title: 1991 AMC 8 Problem 14
statement: Several students are competing in a series of three races. A student earns \(5\) points for winning a race, \(3\) points for finishing second, and \(1\) point for finishing third. There are no ties. What is the smallest number of points that a student must earn in the three races to be guaranteed of earning more points than any other student?

solutions.text:
A total of \(11\) (for example \(5+5+1\)) does not guarantee first place, since another student could also reach \(11.\)

But if one student scores \(5+5+3 = 13,\) the remaining places give every other student at most \(3+3+5 = 11.\) So \(13\) points guarantees the lead.

Thus, the correct answer is D .
hints: To be guaranteed the lead, plan for the worst case where another student does as well as possible
Check the attainable three-race totals in increasing order; for each one, see whether the remaining places allow a rival to tie or exceed it
